title: Explainable_artificial_intelligence
summary:
Explainable AI (XAI), generally overlapping with interpretable AI or explainable machine learning, is a field of research within artificial intelligence that explores methods providing humans with the ability of intellectual oversight over AI algorithms.

In the 2010s, public concerns about racial and other bias in the use of AI for criminal sentencing decisions and findings of creditworthiness led to increased demand for transparent artificial intelligence. DARPA launched its Explainable Artificial Intelligence program in August 2016. The first global conference exclusively dedicated to this discipline was the 2017 International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence Workshop on XAI.

Technical approaches include glass-box models which are more transparent to inspection, such as decision trees, Bayesian networks, and sparse linear models. Some techniques allow visualizations of the inputs to which individual software neurons respond most strongly. Popular methods include SHAP, which enables visualizing the contribution of each feature to the output, and LIME, which can locally approximate a model's outputs with a simpler, interpretable model.

The European Union introduced a right to explanation in the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), implemented in 2018. In the United States, insurance companies are required to be able to explain their rate and coverage decisions. In France, the Digital Republic Act grants subjects the right to request information pertaining to algorithms processing their data. A major challenge is the trade-off between model accuracy and interpretability, as complex models such as deep learning often achieve higher accuracy but are less interpretable, while simpler models offer more transparency at the cost of predictive performance.
